title: GSAP Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this GSAP course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does gsap.to describe?
options: The ending values of a tween
questions.explanation: A tween changes values over time. gsap.to starts from the current value and moves toward the value you give it.

questions.question: Which values are supplied to gsap.from?
questions.explanation: gsap.from starts with the supplied values and moves to the element's current values. It is useful for a simple entrance.

questions.question: Why choose fromTo?
options: To state both start and end values
questions.explanation: fromTo names both the starting and ending values. It helps when neither end should depend on the current style.

questions.question: What does easing change?
options: How speed changes during the tween
questions.explanation: Easing changes the speed during a tween. An out ease slows near the end instead of stopping abruptly.

questions.question: How many plays happen with repeat:1?
questions.explanation: repeat adds more plays after the first. yoyo reverses the direction on alternate plays.

questions.question: When does the second tween start by default?
questions.explanation: A timeline groups tweens in order. By default, a new tween begins after the previous one finishes.

questions.question: What does the < position mean here?
options: Start at the previous tween's start
questions.explanation: A timeline position can make two tweens overlap. The less-than position starts a tween at the previous tween's start.

questions.question: What does stagger control?
options: The gap between starting each item's tween
questions.explanation: Stagger starts similar tweens at slightly different times. It can guide attention across a small group.

questions.question: Why set paused:true?
options: To wait for a playback action
To remove the box from the page
questions.explanation: A tween object has methods to play, pause and reverse. A control can let a reader choose whether motion runs.

questions.question: What happens for a reduced-motion preference here?
options: The box stays visible without the entrance movement
questions.explanation: GSAP matchMedia can choose different motion based on a media query. A reduced-motion preference should get a calmer version.

questions.question: What does context.revert help with?
options: Cleaning up a component's animations and styles
questions.explanation: A GSAP context can collect animations created for a component. Reverting it restores their styles and removes that animation work.

questions.question: What does scale change in this example?
options: The drawn size through a transform
questions.explanation: Transform and opacity animations often avoid redoing page layout. The right choice still depends on the real page and device.
